{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately BEFORE the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The morning Mara left, the valley was wrapped in fog. Her grandmother stood on the porch in her housecoat, one hand lifted against the cold, while the taxi idled beside the gate. Neither of them had slept much. They had spent the night talking around the things they were afraid to say directly.

“You’ll call when you get there,” her grandmother said.

“I will.”

“And write.”

Mara promised that, too. She meant it. She had already bought a packet of stationery, pale blue with little silver stars, and placed it on top of her suitcase. Beneath it lay a book she’d carried through school and college, its cloth cover softened at the corners. She had nearly left it behind, but at the last minute slipped it between her sweaters.

Her grandmother walked her to the taxi. At the gate, Mara hugged her quickly, then again, properly. The driver waited without looking at them. When the car pulled away, her grandmother grew smaller in the rear window, until the fog took her.

The journey lasted most of the day. Mara watched familiar fields give way to rail yards, then to streets packed with buses and people moving as if they already knew where they were going. At the station, she struggled with her suitcase and nearly missed the cab she’d called. By the time she reached the apartment, rain had begun to tap at the windows.

She unpacked only what she needed: a mug, a towel, the book from home. Too tired to read, she set it on the kitchen counter and went to bed among half-open boxes. The city hummed beyond the glass. In the morning, she would start making a life there."}
